cover.title: Probate Lawyer Pay, Set By Law
cover.label: $900K

lines.text: In California, a probate lawyer's pay is written into law.
lines.say: In California, a probate lawyer's pay is written into law.

lines.text: Example: on a $900,000 house, that's $21,000, and a mortgage doesn't shrink it.
lines.say: On a nine hundred thousand dollar house, that's twenty-one thousand dollars, and a mortgage doesn't shrink it.

lines.text: Most states just require a 'reasonable' fee, often hourly. California sets a sliding percentage.
lines.say: Most states just require a reasonable fee, often hourly. California sets a sliding percentage.

lines.text: 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, then 1%.
lines.say: It's four percent of the first hundred thousand, three percent of the next hundred thousand, two percent of the next eight hundred thousand, then one percent.
So nine hundred thousand is four thousand, plus three thousand, plus fourteen thousand: twenty-one thousand dollars.

lines.text: The fee rises with the estate, but the rate falls.
lines.say: The fee rises with the estate, but the rate falls.

lines.text: The twist: it uses gross value. Owe $500,000 on it, and the fee still counts all $900,000.
lines.say: The twist: it uses gross value. Owe five hundred thousand on it, and the fee still counts all nine hundred thousand.

lines.text: The executor can claim the same schedule too: another $21,000.
lines.say: The executor can claim the same schedule too: another twenty-one thousand dollars.

lines.text: Extra work, like a lawsuit, needs a judge's OK. Assets in a living trust skip probate entirely.
lines.say: Extra work, like a lawsuit, needs a judge's okay. Assets in a living trust skip probate entirely.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: In California, a probate lawyer's pay is set by law
post.ig:
In California, a probate lawyer's pay is written into law.

The schedule: 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, then 1%.
Example: a $900,000 house means a $21,000 attorney fee, and the executor can claim another $21,000.
The fee uses gross value, so a mortgage doesn't lower it.

Sources: California Probate Code sections 10800, 10810 and 10811.
